definitions.title: Vector in Three Dimensions
definitions.latex: \mathbf{v} = \langle v_1, v_2, v_3 \rangle = v_1 \mathbf{i} + v_2 \mathbf{j} + v_3 \mathbf{k}
definitions.statement: A three-dimensional vector is an equivalence class of directed line segments having the same length and direction. In component form, v = <v_1, v_2, v_3>, where v_1, v_2, v_3 are the scalar components along the standard basis vectors.
definitions.explanation: Vectors model physical quantities possessing both magnitude and spatial orientation, such as displacement, velocity, and force.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Vectors add component-wise and scale linearly by multiplying each component.

definitions.title: Vector Magnitude and Unit Vector
definitions.statement: The magnitude (or norm) of v is its Euclidean length. A unit vector u in the direction of non-zero v has length 1 and is obtained by dividing v by its magnitude.
conditions: |v| >= 0 with equality if and only if v = 0
definitions.explanation: Normalization isolates direction from magnitude, allowing directional decomposition of vector quantities.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Every non-zero vector decomposes uniquely as v = |v| u.
